topic_candidates.brief: AI can make software appear to move faster while quietly increasing the maintenance bill. This video follows the order of the breakout: the huge AI investment, Claude’s internal coding claim, then the less visible problem of AI systems producing code that nobody fully understands. It explains technical debt with an everyday analogy—borrowing speed now and paying for bugs, tangled dependencies and security fixes later—and ends with what ordinary users may notice: slower updates, outages and more rushed patches.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: A 2026 empirical study examined more than 302,000 verified AI-authored commits across 6,299 GitHub repositories. It identified hundreds of thousands of issues, found that between 7.5% and 14.8% of commits from each assistant introduced at least one issue, and reported that 22.7% of tracked AI-introduced issues remained in the latest revision. These figures support a cautious explanation of AI-related maintenance risk, not a claim that all AI-written code is bad. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2603.28592?trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block&utm_source=openai))
